newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's foreign minister quits over criticism.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's foreign minister quits over criticism.

text.p: Slovenian Foreign Minister Zoran Thaler resigned on Thursday following opposition criticism over his handling of Europe and NATO but Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek urged him to reconsider his decision.
Thaler quit over what he called "impossible" domestic political conditions and for the sake of national unity at a time when Slovenia is preparing to integrate into Europe.
Drnovsek, leader of the centre-left Liberal Democrats, said in a statement that he had asked Thaler to stay on.
"This is a great loss and we hope he will be back with us soon," Liberal Democrat general secretary Gregor Golobic told Slovenian state radio.
Golobic said the party would probably name a candidate as new foreign minister in September if Thaler declined Drnovsek's invitation to remain in office.
Thaler, a member of Drnovsek's Liberal Democrats, has served as foreign minister since February when a new government was formed following an inconclusive general election in November.

Thaler quit as foreign minister once before. He was forced out of office in a parliamentary confidence vote in May 1996 after being accused of botching Slovenia's bid for associate membership of the European Union.
The association accord was finally signed in June 1996.

"Both times while being foreign minister there was a feeling of division due to political and personal interests regardless of the broad national importance of consensus over the key areas of foreign policy," Thaler said.
Thaler has been under growing pressure from the opposition centre-left Social Democrats which last week called for a parliamentary debate on the government's performance.
The debate is expected to take place in September and could lead to a no-confidence vote in the coalition government which holds only 49 out of 90 parliamentary seats.
The Social Democrats have accused Thaler of being partly responsible for Slovenia having to change the constitution to allow foreigners to buy land in accordance with the EU accord.

The Social Democrats and opposition Christian Democrats have also accused Thaler of failing to win Slovenia a place in the first group of ex-communist countries invited to join an enlarged NATO in 1999.
